title: San Francisco made voucher payments after required inspection follow-up was missed

beats.text: When a voucher unit fails inspection, a second clock starts.

visual.sub: The issue was what happened after a home failed inspection

beats.text: Owners generally had 24 hours for life-threatening defects.
Other defects generally had thirty days or an approved extension.

visual.label: Other defects, unless an extension was approved

visual.kicker: Thirteen of 60 FY2019 cases lacked the follow-up inspection and the abatement notice

beats.text: Thirteen cases had neither the follow-up inspection nor the payment suspension notice.

visual.kicker: Thirteen of 60 FY2019 cases lacked the follow-up inspection and the abatement notice

beats.text: The 2020 audit questioned $110,628 after failures in another sample.

visual.kicker: The next sample questioned $110,628, and a later audit reported implementation

beats.text: A subsequent audit recorded corrective action on the 2021 finding.

visual.kicker: The next sample questioned $110,628, and a later audit reported implementation

beats.text: Then three cases in 2023 raised the issue again.

visual.kicker: A later recurrence ended with evidence that sampled homes passed

beats.text: In 2024 eight sampled homes had late follow-up but eventually passed.
Auditors questioned no payment for those homes and later reported implementation.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
